programme.title: The Tenpenny Files - How Does God Use Suffering for Our Good - Pastor Clay Jones and Jean E Jones
programme.desc:
Do the heartbreaks losses medical crises and relational fractures of life carry meaning Does suffering hold depth that shapes the soul Pastor Clay Jones and Jean Jones confront that question through miscarriage infertility foster parenting high-needs children cancer and major surgery They present suffering as God’s chosen instrument for forming character and preparing believers for eternity “No one gets through this life without immense suffering” That statement sets the tone Suffering is not rare It is inevitable The issue is not its presence The issue is its purpose “How has suffering impacted your own life” Jean reaches a place many believers quietly fear She begins to ask whether she is angry at God Five miscarriages force her to confront entitlement grief and surrender She describes placing her pain before the cross as an offering She describes learning to trust without explanation Clay makes a claim that unsettles comfort “God’s plan A for your life is to take you through regular periods of suffering There is no plan B” He connects endurance to character He connects character to hope He speaks from bone cancer and open heart surgery He speaks from experience that refuses sentiment Hard questions surface Is turning to medical care a lack of faith How do you weigh quality of life against quantity of life What do you say when someone cries How do you remember God’s past faithfulness when fresh hardship reopens old wounds This conversation does not attempt to remove the weight of suffering It asks what suffering is producing Does suffering as they describe it function as formation within God’s larger design
